tx: 0:00 How did the United States defeat Japan | 0:02 during World War II? While Nazi Germany | 0:04 was pushing forward in Europe, its ally | 0:06 Japan was occupying lands in Asia. In | 0:09 41, Japan attacked Pearl Harbor, a | 0:11 military base in Hawaii, and started the | 0:13 war with the United States. This | 0:15 surprise air strike disabled part of the | 0:17 American Navy and gave Japan a temporary | 0:19 advantage in the Pacific. But the US | 0:21 recovered quickly and after their | 0:23 victory in the 4-day Battle of Midway, | 0:25 where several Japanese aircraft carriers | 0:27 were destroyed, they retook the | 0:28 initiative. From that point, the US | 0:30 began an island hopping strategy, | 0:32 methodically cutting off Japanese supply | 0:34 lines, weakening their forces and | 0:36 capturing one island after another as | 0:38 they approached Japan itself. As Nazi | 0:41 Germany fell, the US won one of the | 0:43 bloodiest battles in the Pacific, the | 0:44 Battle of Okinawa, which showed that the | 0:46 Japanese had no intention of | 0:48 surrendering. Given the huge losses and | 0:50 fierce Japanese resistance, the US made | 0:53 the decision to use atomic bombs on | 0:54 Hiroshima and Nagasaki, after which | 0:57 Japan surrendered and World War II soon | 0:59 officially ended.
